const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(value, key);
        if (descriptor !== undefined && !descriptor.enumerable) {
evidence.reason: In `src/shared/jsonLossless.ts`, the own-member loop (lines 86-98) only rejects symbol keys and descriptors where `!descriptor.enumerable` (lines 90-91). An *enumerable accessor* descriptor has `enumerable: true` and no `value` property, so it passes this guard. The value is then read via `Object.values(value)` at line 99, which invokes the getter once; the subsequent `JSON.stringify` invokes the same getter again. Because these are independent reads, a non-deterministic getter can make the value the walk validates differ from the value stringified — e.g. hiding a lossy `NaN`/`Infinity` that stringify converts to `null`, or returning a different valid value on the second read. The array branch has the same hole: lines 50-57 `continue` for valid integer indices without inspecting their descriptors, and line 65 reads `value[i]`, invoking an index getter that stringify will invoke again. This is an implementation gap in the module's stated lossless invariant (the comments at lines 76-85 explicitly reason about JSON.stringify/walk divergence), not a new requirement. The smallest compatible repair is to require data descriptors: reject when `descriptor !== undefined && !('value' in descriptor)` at lines 90-91, and likewise check each element's descriptor before reading it at line 65. This is a local correctness fix, not a disruptive or architectural change.
